name: Foma Fomapan 200 Creative
notes: Foma datasheet 'FOMAPAN 200 Creative', 2 pages, vector (page 1: data and plots; page 2: development time curves). No publication number is printed; the date is the footer code 'FOMA 05/22' on page 2. Speed ISO 200/24 deg (24 deg CSN), panchromatic, T-crystal emulsion.

curves: page 1, 'Characteristic curves', exposure Daylight 5500 K, 1/20 s, developer Microphen at 20 C, three curves 1 = 4 min, 2 = 6 min, 3 = 8 min. x axis is 'Log rel. exposure' (relative, no absolute lux-seconds; -3 is at the left frame edge, -2 and -1 on grid lines, 0 at the right frame edge), y is density (0 to 3). Curves are traced from the vector paths; they start at the left frame edge (log rel. exposure -3.0) and stop at about -0.35 (D 2.10, 2.60, 2.94).

v is the 6 min curve: the sheet lists Microphen stock 5-6 min at 20 C (6 min is the plotted time inside that range); the page 2 gamma-time plot for Microphen 20 C reaches gamma 0.6 (the granularity condition) at about 4.5 min, which would point to the 4 min curve, so the choice of v is a judgement. The others are v-microphen-4 and v-microphen-8 (8 min is well outside the recommended range). The sheet marks no curve as standard.

The three curve drawings are numerically identical to the three curves in the Fomapan 100 Classic sheet (same density at every log H; there labelled 5, 7, 11 min), only the time labels differ, so they may be a reused drawing rather than a measurement of this film. Traced as printed.

sensitivity: page 1, 'Relative spectral sensitivity (wedge spectrogram at 2850 K)', a plotted curve (vector) with axis label S-lambda and no numbers or units on the y axis, so it is not known whether it is linear or logarithmic. y here is the fraction of the frame height (0 = bottom of the frame, 1 = top), nothing more; do not read it as log sensitivity without checking. x grid lines every 50 nm; the printed labels sit about 6 pt right of their lines and the lines are taken as 400, 500, 600, 700 nm (labels are not centred on the lines, so the wavelength scale is uncertain by up to about 10 nm). The curve starts at 400 nm (frame edge), peaks near 685 nm and falls in a straight steep line to the frame bottom at about 716 nm.

Grain: RMS 14.0 (Microphen at 20 C, developed to gamma = 0.6, measured at D = 1.0); aperture not stated. Resolving power 110 lines/mm. Schwarzschild effect table and development time table (Microphen stock 5-6 min at 20 C, 2 min at 30 C) on page 1.
